recipes.name: Kale Pesto Pasta
ingredients: 4 cups tightly packed (100g) kale leaves (, torn by hand, about 4 stems (curly kale or Cavolo nero/lacinto) - Note 1)
1/2 cup tightly packed (50g) finely grated parmesan (, store bought sandy-type from fridge is fine here, else grate your own - Note 2)
1 garlic clove (, minced using garlic press)
1/2 cup (50g) walnuts ( - substitute cashews or almonds, or halve the quantity for pine nuts)
1/2 cup (125 ml) extra virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes (, for slight warmth - feel free to reduce, or omit (substitute with black pepper))
500g / 1 lb pasta of choice ( - long or short (pictured: Casarecce N.88))
2 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (, for pasta cooking water)
1/3 cup reserved pasta cooking water (, for pasta tossing)
instructions: Toast walnuts, pour into bowl with all pesto ingredients, blitz until finely puréed. Toss with hot pasta and with 1/3 cup pasta cooking water.
Cook pasta - Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the 2 teaspoons of salt. Add the pasta and cook for the time per the packet directions.
Reserve water - Just before draining, scoop out 1 cup of pasta cooking water. Then drain the pasta and return into the pasta cooking pot.
Toast walnuts - Heat a small pan over medium high heat (no oil). Add the walnuts and toast for 3 minutes, tossing every now and then, until it has light brown spots and it smells nutty.

Blitz pesto - Immediately pour the walnuts into a large bowl (no need to cool, can blitz while hot). Add remaining pesto ingredients. Blitz using a stick blender until the kale is as finely blitzed as you can, about 20 - 30 seconds. It won't turn into a smoothie (kale is hardy!). (Note 3 on food processor)

Toss with pasta - Pour over the hot pasta and add 1/3 cup of the reserved pasta cooking water. Toss well until evenly coated, using extra pasta cooking water as needed to loosen, then serve immediately garnished with extra parmesan. It's especially nice hot (brings out the garlic and parmesan flavour) though also lovely served as a cold pasta salad.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Kale – You’ll need 4 curly kale stems, about 30cm/12″ long (measuring leafy part only, not naked stem). To measure the kale, push the kale leaves into a measuring cup quite firmly. Or use scales – easier! The recipe is quite forgiving – so if you use too much kale you’ll know as the pesto will be too thick and dry – just add extra oil. If too little, too loose and oily, just add more kale leaves (or baby spinach, if you’re out of kale). To remove kale leaves , grip the stem, close your fist loosely around the leaves and slide your hand up to rip the leaves off. Then use your hands to tear into pieces. Other leafy greens – Any leafy greens will in theory work here, like baby spinach, English spinach, silverbeet (chard), collard greens. I wouldn’t use frozen though as they are too wet to blitz. 2. Parmesan substitute (non-dairy) – Anchovies! Terrific flavour booster, like used in Caesar Dressing . Start with a modest amount, blitz, taste, then add more if desired. 3. Blitzing tool – I find the stick blender most effective, you can move it around, there’s no need to scrape down the sides, and it really purees up the hardy kale well. If using a food processor, you’ll need to scrape down the sides quite a few times but it still won’t puree it quite as well as a stick blender can. Leftovers will keep for 2 days, beyond this I find the fresh flavours start to fade. The pesto can also be frozen for up to 3 months in an airtight container (I wouldn’t freeze on the pasta, just the pesto by itself). Nutrition per serving, assuming 5 servings.
